chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Uthman narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Tusi narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Aslam narrated to us, he said: Al-Hakam from Sa'id ibn Bashir from Qatadah from Anas ibn Malik, who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever fasts Ramadan, concludes it with charity, and goes to the prayer place after taking a ritual bath, he will return forgiven.'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for forgiveness mentioned in the hadith regarding fasting Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal* highlights the synergistic value of combining fasting, charity (Sadaqah), and ritual purity (Ghusl) to secure divine forgiveness. It reflects the Shia emphasis on the holistic nature of worship, where physical acts of devotion are complemented by spiritual preparation and charitable deeds to maximize reward at the conclusion of Ramadan.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) says, “One who fasts during the  month  of  Ramadan,  ends  it  with  charity  and  goes  to prayer-mat  after  taking  ritual  bath  he  would  be  forgiven before   he gets up from the prayer-mat.”
